abilities.name: Attack
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target.
abilities._source: Convention: every class ships a free rank-1 Attack.

abilities.name: Infernal Strike
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target. Generates 20 Deathfire.
abilities._source: CoA: 'weave a cheap filler strike in Infernal Strike, which generates 2 Demonfire'. The universal filler, on Warrior's heroic_strike curve.

abilities.name: Sever
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target. Generates 10 Deathfire.
abilities._source: CoA: 'using Sever to top up rage'. Cheapest strike in the kit, so it is the one you press when the pool is empty.

abilities.name: Meatsaw
abilities.description: Deals damage to up to 3 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Meatsaw (hits nearby enemies)'. target_type enemy_aoe + max_targets is what the engine actually reads for a limited cleave; the is_aoe flag is never read at load time.

abilities.name: Skulltaker
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target.
abilities._source: CoA: 'dump stacked Demonfire into Skulltaker for its scaling finisher: more damage per stack'. The class's single-target Deathfire spender, shared by all three specs. 40 Deathfire is CoA's 4-stack spend.

abilities.name: Suffuse
abilities.description: Heals you.
abilities._source: CoA: 'You spend Demonfire on Suffuse, an instant self-heal that scales off Stamina and defensive stats, so you top yourself off constantly as a side effect of pressing your rotation.' Frontier heals scale off healing_power, not Stamina or defense rating, so the Stamina scaling is lost; the Deathfire-funded self-sustain loop, which is the actual identity, is intact. VALUE RESOLVED 2026-10-29: this script and the shipped JSON disagreed - data had cost 30 / effect_value 150-570, this script had cost 50 / 60-216 - which means one side was edited and the other never re-run. Kept THESE values because they sit in the peer band for a single-target self-heal (Paladin Holy Light 52-162, Priest Heal 54-166, Shaman Healing Wave 56-171) while the data's 150 at rank 1 was roughly 3x that AND cheaper. A one-line revert if the 30/150 table was deliberate.

abilities.name: Melt
abilities.description: Deals Fire damage to the target over time for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA names Melt beside Infernal Strike and Meatsaw in 'A Gift from Hell' (the Rage-cost cut) and in 'Infernal Pummeling', which makes it the target's damage amp. The burn half is what the engine can express, so it is a Fire DoT.

abilities.name: Flames of Xoroth
abilities.description: Deals Fire damage to up to 4 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Your AoE comes from Flames of Xoroth'. Present in all three specs (War transforms it into Warbringer, Defiance into Hellfire Bellows).

abilities.name: Flesh Hook
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Flesh Hook (pulls the enemy to you)', 'Flesh Hook is your only reach tool'. ranged_damage - it is thrown. The engine has no forced-reposition mechanic, so the pull itself is flavour.

abilities.name: Chainwhip
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Swing a chain at an enemy dealing Physical damage and silencing them for 2 seconds, generating a large amount of threat.' The engine has no silence category (see StatusEffect.is_stun, the only incapacitate), so the damage and its threat are what lands.

abilities.name: Chains of Malice
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target and stuns it.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Lock an enemy down with magical chains, stunning them and dragging them with you for 5 seconds.' The stun is real; the drag is not modellable.

abilities.name: Dread
abilities.description: Threat generated +180% for 2 turns.
abilities._source: The class tree's Dread, which is the one node whose tooltip the scrape could not capture ('(see builder tooltip)'), so the MECHANIC here is Frontier's choice rather than CoA's: the kit otherwise has no taunt, and Defiance is a main tank. Implemented as a threat_generation_pct buff, the convention Guardian's Challenging Cry (200) and Cultist's Twilight Domain (180) already use - ability buff stat_mods are percent POINTS here, unlike talent effects, which are fractions.

abilities.name: Black Shield
abilities.description: Strengthens you for 3 turns, absorbing damage.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Consume all of your Demon's Blood stacks to create a demonic shield that absorbs 860 damage, increased by 20% per Demon's Blood stack'. Demon's Blood has no engine hook, so the absorb is a flat share of max health instead of a stack-scaled number.

abilities.name: Demon Heart
abilities.description: Restores rage to you. Generates 20 Deathfire.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Embrace your inner demon, instantly generating 6 stacks of Demonfire and 50 Rage.' Both halves are real: restore_resource refills Rage (off the rank's mana_restore_pct, which is where the engine reads the amount) and `generates` pays the Deathfire.

abilities.name: Burning Rage
abilities.description: Immune to crowd control, Haste +10 for 2 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Enrage, generating 15 Rage every 1 sec and making you immune to incapacitate, banish, and polymorph effects for 6 seconds. Usable while incapacitated.' cc_immune is a real stat_mod the engine checks before applying an incapacitate. The Rage-per-second half belongs to Demon Heart instead - one ability cannot both buff and restore.

abilities.name: Juggernaut
abilities.description: Damage taken -25% for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Consume all of your Demon's Blood to become a juggernaut, reducing all damage taken by 30% for 10 seconds.' The tick-healing half and the Demon's Blood cost are not modellable; -25% for 3 turns on a 12-turn cooldown sits just under Warrior's Shield Wall (-40%, 2 turns) deliberately, since every spec gets this one.

abilities.name: Unleash Pestilence
abilities.description: Deals damage to up to 5 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Unleashes your active Pestilence to trigger a powerful effect.' Which Pestilence is up changes what it does in CoA; the engine has no such branch, so it is one AoE burst regardless.

abilities.name: Pestilence of Death
abilities.description: Physical crit chance +8, Spell crit chance +8.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Emanate a pestilence, increasing your critical damage by 10%.' No buff-sourced crit-DAMAGE key exists (crit_damage_physical is read off talents only), so it grants crit CHANCE instead. One Pestilence at a time, so the two share an exclusive_group.

abilities.name: Pestilence of Apocalypse
abilities.description: The air around you turns thin and hot, and everything in it burns easier.
abilities._source: CoA: 'causing targets within 8 yds to take 10% increased Fire damage from you'. The engine has no per-enemy aura; damage_dealt_pct on the Knight is the same arithmetic from the other side.

abilities.name: Shieldgore
abilities.description: Put the spikes of your shield through them. It is the loudest thing you can do.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Transforms your Infernal Strike into Shieldgore. Generates 2 Demonfire. Gore the target with your spiked shield, causing High Threat Fire Damage, scaling with your block value.' Block-value scaling has no hook on the damage path, so the damage is flat; the Deathfire generation and the threat from a big hit are what the spec's whole loop actually runs on.

abilities.name: Call: Hellfire Imp
abilities.description: Summons a pet to fight for you. Generates 20 Rage.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Beckon 1 Hellfire Imp to aid you in battle for 12 seconds and generate 20 Rage. Threat generated by Hellfire Imps is transferred to you.' CoA calls it 'a free rage battery that also summons a body', so the Rage is the generates payload. NOW ITS OWN TEMPLATE: this reused the Warlock's 'imp' and summoned a pet named Imp, which was the most defensible of the mismatches fixed in Oct 2026 - an imp summoning an Imp. It was split out anyway because CoA names the creature (Call: Hellfire Abyssal's own tooltip reads 'Costs 15 less Rage for each active Hellfire Imp') and because this class's Summon: Greater Imp now has a real template of its own, so leaving this one on the Warlock's roster would have given one class an 'Imp' and a 'Greater Imp' from two different places with the Warlock's fire numbers underneath. 'hellfire_imp' is deliberately much weaker than the Warlock Imp it replaced - Knight of Xoroth's called demons are a side channel, not its damage identity.

abilities.name: Call: Hellfire Abyssal
abilities.description: Summons a pet to fight for you.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Call down a Hellfire Abyssal from the sky to crash down upon the targeted 8 yd area, dealing AP Fire damage. The abyssal remains to aid you in battle for 15 seconds and emits an aura that reduces the damage taken by party and raid members within 40 yds by 5%.' NOW A REAL ABYSSAL: this used to borrow voidwalker and summoned a pet named Voidwalker, picked as the tankiest demon then in pet_templates.py. The template now exists - the slowest and most armoured of this class's three called demons, with a real Fire signature. The party aura is still carried by the capstone NODE that unlocks this, which remains the only place the engine can express it: a pet-cast party buff resolves onto the pet alone, which the template's _source spells out.

abilities.name: Implosion
abilities.description: Deals Fire damage to up to 5 targets. Generates 30 Rage.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Explode with hellish fire, dealing Fire damage to nearby enemies, beckoning Hellfire Imps to aid you in battle, and generating 30 Rage. Deals increased damage ... for each Demonfire consumed.' Spends Deathfire and pays Rage, which is the one place the class's two pools trade in that direction. The imp summon cannot ride along on a damage ability.

abilities.name: Sacrificial Circle
abilities.description: Heals you.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Sacrifice your Hellfire Imps within 15 yds, healing you 15% of your maximum health, plus an additional amount equal to 25% of each of your Hellfire Imp's maximum health.' The engine cannot consume your own pets as a cost, so it is a flat emergency heal on a long cooldown. The Soul Furnace absorb that CoA leaves behind is the Defiance node of that name.

abilities.name: Curse of Xoroth
abilities.description: Deals Fire/Shadow damage to the target over time for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Curse an enemy for 15 seconds, dealing Shadowflame Damage over 15 seconds. Your next Shieldgore within 12 seconds grants you Black Shield.' There is no shadowflame school; the engine supports a COMBINED school list (Sun Cleric's Radiant Flame is ['holy', 'fire']), so Fire plus Shadow is literal. The Black Shield priming is not modellable.

abilities.name: Chains of Xoroth
abilities.description: Applies to all nearby enemies: Haste -20 for 2 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Create demonic chains at target location that slow enemies inside by -80% for 5 seconds. At the end of the duration, it pulls all affected enemies to it.' The slow is real; the terminal pull is not. Same haste-negative snare shape Guardian's Net Throw uses.

abilities.name: Hellfire Bellows
abilities.description: Deals Fire damage to up to 4 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Transforms your Flames of Xoroth into Hellfire Bellows. Bellow fire on all enemies in a 6 yd cone in front of and behind you.' Frontier has no facing, so the cone is a capped cleave.

abilities.name: Legion's Presence
abilities.description: Grants your party: Damage dealt +10% for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Emanate an aura to allies within 25 yds for 15 seconds, increasing their damage dealt by 10%.' target_type party is what makes a buff land on allies; buff_scope only chooses between a 30-minute raid buff and a turn-based combat one.

abilities.name: Gore
abilities.description: Deals damage to the target. Generates 10 Deathfire.
abilities._source: CoA: '2 Charges, 8 sec recharge. Generates 1 Demonfire. Quickly gore an enemy.' Charges have no engine equivalent, so it is a 2-turn cooldown. CoA gates Gore behind two maxed War talents, so it is talent-unlocked here too.

abilities.name: Warbringer
abilities.description: Deals damage to up to 4 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Transforms your Flames of Xoroth into Warbringer. Slam the ground, dealing Weapon Damage to nearby enemies, reducing the effectiveness of any healing by -50% for 10 seconds.' A damage ability cannot also apply a debuff, so the anti-heal is lost here; healing_taken_pct exists but only on a debuff ability, and War's own page calls the cleave the point.

abilities.name: Brimstone Bludgeon
abilities.description: Deals damage to up to 4 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Walking in and popping Brimstone Bludgeon is the opener: heavy weapon damage to the pack that also unleashes Pestilence of Death'. The spec's keystone and its tier-6 pick, so it is unlocked by the capstone node. The Pestilence unleash is a separate button here.

abilities.name: Decimation
abilities.description: Physical crit chance +40 for 2 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Your next Skulltaker or Warbringer is guaranteed to critically strike for 25% increased damage.' Nothing can guarantee a crit or restrict a buff to the next cast of two named abilities, so it is a large crit window instead - the same shape as Warrior's Recklessness (crit_chance_physical 100).

abilities.name: Burning Blade
abilities.description: Armor Penetration Pct +30%, Attack Power +40 for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Ignite your weapon, causing you to send out searing fire with each melee critical strike, dealing Fire damage in a line and increasing your Armor penetration by 30% while active.' The armour penetration is literal; the on-crit fire line is the War tree's Hellsmelted node.

abilities.name: Searing Blade
abilities.description: Deals Fire damage to the target.
abilities._source: CoA names Searing Blade in War's Domination ('Melee critical strikes now reduce the cooldown of Searing Blade'), which is all the reference says about it, so it is authored as the spec's mid-cooldown Fire strike.

abilities.name: Seeking Flame
abilities.description: The fire goes and finds them. It is slower to leave than to arrive.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Generates 1 Demonfire. Sear an enemy, dealing Fire damage', and 'Seeking Flame's slow keeps targets in reach'. The engine has no slow on a damage ability, so the slow is lost and the Deathfire generation is the mechanical half.

abilities.name: Hellmaw
abilities.description: Deals Fire/Shadow damage to the target over time for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Burn an enemy with a fiery strike, dealing Shadowflame Damage, plus an additional amount over 12 seconds. Deals 20% increased damage per Demonfire consumed.' Hellmaw is a Hellfire tree pick in CoA, so it is talent-unlocked. Shadowflame is the combined ['fire', 'shadow'] school.

abilities.name: Hellfire Form
abilities.description: Damage dealt +20%, Spell crit chance +15 for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Enter your Hellfire Form, increasing your Fire damage dealt by 20% and Fire critical strike chance by 15% for 15 seconds', 'the Metamorphosis-style transformation cooldown'. Not effect_type shapeshift: combat/forms.py is a shared file and has no Hellfire Form, so it is a buff. damage_dealt_pct is school-agnostic in this engine, so the Fire restriction is lost.

abilities.name: Hellstorm
abilities.description: Deals Fire damage to up to 6 targets.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Create a hellstorm, dealing Fire damage to up to 8 nearby enemies. Embers then flare every 1 sec ... Duration is increased by 100% for each stack of Demonfire consumed.' The ember ticks would need a damage ability that also lays a DoT, which the engine does not have, so it is one large capped AoE hit.

abilities.name: Summon: Greater Imp
abilities.description: Summons a pet to fight for you.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Teaches you Summon: Greater Imp ... Greater Imp has various combat abilities that provide excellent single target damage and control.' NOW A REAL GREATER IMP: this used to borrow felhunter and summoned a pet named Felhunter, picked as the demon with a real single-target kit. The template now exists, tuned up against this class's own Hellfire Imp rather than down from the Warlock's Felhunter, since 'excellent single target damage' is the brief. The 'control' half is not authored - every control shape here is a debuff or the is_stun flag, and a pet never casts a debuff. CoA makes this a free level-10 passive of the Hellfire tree; Frontier has no free passives, so it is an ordinary summon the whole class can train.
